description: SECURITY (s440). A client fn wraps a server-fn call in a helper declared INSIDE it (`function inner(x) { return isOk(x) }`) and uses the helper in a `.some` callback. The server fn answers false for every element, so `.some` MUST be false and the verdict "rejected". Before s440 the nested helper was emitted `async` but called as if sync — `.some` saw one Promise per element, always truthy, and answered TRUE for every input ("accepted": an accept-all), with no diagnostic. A nested async helper is now awaited exactly like a file-scope one (the clean-family callback is lifted to the async combinator).
rationale: §13.2: the compiler SHALL insert `await` at every call site where a server-generated fetch call is made, and SHALL wrap any function containing a server call in an `async` function. `inner` contains one, so `inner` is async, and every call to it is a server call site that must be awaited. A position where the await cannot be inserted must fail closed (E-SERVER-FN-IN-SYNC-CALLBACK, §34); a `.some` callback is lifted to an awaited combinator, so here the program runs and the answer is the server's answer.
